AI Engineering T oolkit MCP Servers & Companion T ools Beyond Claude Code’s Core Docs Context7 was one example. This is the wider map: what exists, what it’s for , and when to actually reach for it instead of building something yourself. Why this matters Claude Code’s own docs cover the mechanism (MCP , skills, hooks). They don’t catalog the ecosystem that’s grown on top of it. As of 2026 there are 17,000+ public MCP servers. Most of what you need already exists — the skill is knowing when to reach for one, not building it. 2

1. Documentation & Context Servers These fix one specific problem: a model’s training data goes stale, but library APIs keep changing. Instead of guessing, the model asks a server for the current answer . Server What it does Add it Context7 (Upstash) Fetches current, version-specific docs for any popular library straight into context claude mcp add --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp DeepWiki MCP Lets Claude ask natural-language questions against any GitHub repo’s structure and code, not just search it Connect via the DeepWiki-hosted MCP endpoint Ref (ref.tools) Alternative to Context7, similar doc-search-into-context approach Hosted HTTP endpoint, add like any remote server When to use one : any time you catch Claude confidently writing code against an API version

e server When to use one : any time you catch Claude confidently writing code against an API version that’s since changed, or hallucinating a method that doesn’t ex- ist. Append use context7 (or the equivalent trigger phrase) to the prompt, or put a standing rule in CLAUDE.md: “always use context7 for library-specific ques- tions.” 3

2. Database & RAG-Specific Servers Directly relevant if you’re building a RAG pipeline — these let Claude inspect and query the actual retrieval layer instead of you copy-pasting schema or query results into chat. Server What it does Postgres / DBHub Natural-language queries, schema exploration, read-only by design when you scope the connection string Supabase MCP Official server — schema, queries, auth config, storage, all from one connection Pinecone MCP Inspect indexes, run similarity queries, check embedding stats directly from a session Chroma MCP Same idea for a local/self-hosted Chroma vector store Weaviate MCP Same idea for Weaviate deployments Vectara MCP Managed semantic-search-as-a-service, exposed as retrieval tools rather than raw vector ops Practical pattern for a RAG

arch-as-a-service, exposed as retrieval tools rather than raw vector ops Practical pattern for a RAG project : connect your vector DB’s MCP server , then ask Claude directly — “show me the top 5 chunks retrieved for this query and their similarity scores” — instead of writing a one-off debug script every time you want to inspect retrieval quality . Use a read-only credential in any database connection string you hand to an MCP server . Claude’s queries should never be able to write to production data unless that is explicitly the point. 4

3. Web Data & Scraping Server What it does Firecrawl MCP Search, scrape, crawl, and structure live web pages into clean data for an agent — keyless trial available, API key for full access Playwright MCP Full browser automation — navigate, click, fill forms, read rendered output Puppeteer MCP Similar browser automation, older/more established tooling When to use one : your agent needs live data that isn’t in any API — competi- tor pricing, a page behind JavaScript rendering, or you’re testing your own web app’s actual rendered behavior (relevant for your mobile-optimization and plat- form work). 5

4. Dev Workflow & Issue T racking Server What it does GitHub MCP Repos, PRs, commits, issues — permission-aware, the same access level as your token Linear MCP Create/update issues, query sprint status, from inside a coding session Jira / Confluence (Atlassian official) 46+ tools across issue tracking and documentation search Notion MCP Read/write workspace pages and databases as live context Sentry MCP Pull error and monitoring data directly into a debugging session — no more copy-pasting stack traces When to use one : the trigger from your reference PDF still applies — “you keep copying data from a tab Claude can’t see.” 6

5. Observability for Agentic Pipelines This is the category most relevant to what you’re actually building — a multi- step agent pipeline is much harder to debug than a single Claude Code session, because you need to see why a chain of steps produced a bad output. Tool What it does MCP? LangSmith Tracing, evaluation, and dataset management for multi-step LLM chains No — standalone platform Langfuse Open-source alternative to LangSmith — tracing, prompt management, cost tracking No — standalone, self-hostable Arize Phoenix Open-source tracing via OpenTelemetry; plugs directly into the Agent SDK’s instrumentation hooks No — OTel-based None of these are MCP servers — they’re the standard tooling for answering “which step in my agent pipeline actually went wrong” once you move past inter-
ooling for answering “which step in my agent pipeline actually went wrong” once you move past inter- active Claude Code sessions into production agents built with the Agent SDK. 7

6. Orchestration Frameworks (complementary, not MCP) If you’re building agent logic that lives outside Claude Code entirely — a sched- uled pipeline, a backend service — these are the frameworks people reach for alongside or instead of the raw Agent SDK: Framework What it’s for LangChain General-purpose LLM app framework — chains, memory , tool-calling abstractions LangGraph Graph-based control flow for multi-step/multi-agent systems, built by the LangChain team LlamaIndex RAG-specific — indexing, retrieval, and query engines, often paired with an MCP layer on top Where the Agent SDK fits relative to these : the SDK gives you Claude Code’s own agent loop, tools, and context management as a library . LangChain/LangGraph/LlamaIndex are model-agnostic frameworks you’d reach for if you want

a library . LangChain/LangGraph/LlamaIndex are model-agnostic frameworks you’d reach for if you want more explicit control over multi-agent graph structure, or need to swap models later . For most single-agent production pipelines built around Claude specifically , the Agent SDK alone (chapter 18 of your Claude Code reference) is the simpler starting point. 8

7. Decision T able — What Do I Actually Need? You’re building… Reach for A coding assistant that needs current library docs Context7 or Ref A RAG chatbot’s retrieval debugging Your vector DB’s MCP server (Pinecone/Chroma/Weaviate) An agent that needs live web data Firecrawl or Playwright MCP A dev-workflow copilot (PRs, issues, docs) GitHub + Linear/Jira + Notion MCP A production agent pipeline you need to debug Langfuse or Arize Phoenix, wired into the Agent SDK A multi-agent system with complex branching logic outside Claude Code LangGraph or a dynamic workflow (see chapter 10) Something that already has 17,000 existing servers doing it Search before you build — check the Anthropic Directory or a marketplace first 9

8. Quick Setup Reference # Documentation claude mcp add --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp # Database (read-only credential!) claude mcp add --transport stdio db -- npx -y @bytebase/dbhub \ --dsn "postgresql://readonly:pass@host:5432/dbname" # GitHub claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ \ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT" # Web scraping claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_FIRECRAWL_KEY" Verify any connection with /mcp before relying on it — check that it shows con- nected, not just that the add command printed success. 10

One caution worth repeating Every server on this list can read data into Claude’s context, and some can act on your behalf (create issues, run queries, push commits). Verify you trust a server before connecting it — a server that fetches external content, including documentation servers, is a potential prompt-injection vector . Scope credentials to read-only wherever the task allows it, especially for anything touching produc- tion data. 11
